problems.note: The narration says "1/6" aloud. Device TTS may read this as "one six" or "1 slash 6", which a child who can't read won't follow. Say "one sixth" in the narration, and keep the 1/6 notation for the screen only.

Narration "1/5 of a pizza or 1/3 of a pizza" depends on fraction notation that TTS may not read clearly. Spell out "one fifth" and "one third" in the narration. Consider also a picture-free cue, since the item has no picture.

Four spoken fractions (1/3, 1/10, 1/5, 1/2) are hard to follow by ear. Spell out the names (one third, one tenth, and so on) in the narration and the choices. Also, 1/10 is a stretch for Grade 1, so consider whether this difficulty-3 item is too hard.
Card 5 reads "One eighth", "One fourth" and "One half" in words, which is good. Keep the same spoken form in items that use numerals like 1/5, 1/6 and 1/10 so the story and items match by ear.
